edit.description: The one home, and the proof the job is already duplicated: `root_reachable_binding` (:1155) and `graph.rs`'s private `bound` (tests/it/graph.rs:2229) build the same root selection over one `reachable` clause, down to near-verbatim doc comments ('the opt-in the judge locates … `members` stays empty: the predicate ranges over `by_kind`'), with this one the degenerate twin — severity fixed at `Required`, no guidance. 18c81f2d gave the `Clause` and the `Contract` host one home each; the `Selection` host is the third and was not in that census. Add a one-clause `Selection` builder over `(selector, severity, predicate, members)` plus the clause's optional guidance — needed by exactly one call site (graph.rs:2599), so an `Option<&str>` parameter or a guidance-carrying variant are both fine — labelling through `labelled_clause` (:1056) with the owner segment derived from the selector: `Selector::Root` takes `temper::contract::ROOT_OWNER`, `Selector::Kind(k)` takes `k`. `Selector::OptIn` is deliberately not derived: a requirement's clause owner is `contract::requirement_owner` (src/contract.rs:109), a different join, and no caller here binds a clause to an opt-in selection — the same 'a proof needing another locus calls the engine directly' fence `one_clause_admissibility` (:1117) already states. `root_reachable_binding` keeps its signature and delegates, so its two callers (tests/it/installed_plugin_kind.rs:140, tests/it/known_marketplace_kind.rs:132) are untouched. Do not reach for `engine::Selector::label` (src/engine.rs:667): it answers the finding's `artifact`, agrees with the label owner only for `Kind` and `Root`, and is private.

Two of the spellings. `bound(severity, guidance)` (:2229) keeps its signature and delegates to the home, so its 12 call sites are untouched; the inline `other` selection (:2641) — a root selection over one `count` clause, built to prove the reachability judge's opt-in guard ignores a foreign predicate — calls the home directly. Both labels (`root.reachable`, `root.count`) are unchanged by the fold: `Reachable` and `Count` name no field, so the derived owner.predicate join reproduces each hand-spelled string exactly.

Two more, with members. `quiet` (:575) is a kind selection over one `count` clause and the second element of `declared` (:596) one over a `reached-from` clause; both call the home. `declared`'s first element is an `OptIn` selection carrying `clauses: Vec::new()` — no clause, so no label and no owner to derive — and stays a literal. `skill.reached-from` (:605) is reproduced by the derived join (`ReachedFrom` names no field, src/contract.rs:903) so the fold changes no byte of it; that it is also not the address a real lock stamps is out of scope here — `reached-from` is one of the four predicates whose emitted `field` column the SDK synthesizes from the roots and via set (`clauseField`, sdk/src/declarations.ts:207), and that two-segment address is pinned on the writer's own side (sdk/test/contract.test.ts:437, sdk/test/emit.test.ts:440).

The sixth spelling. `selection(unit, max, members)` (:47) builds a kind selection over the one whole-grain `extent` clause its local `clause` (:32) already routes through `common::labelled_clause`; it keeps the predicate-building job and delegates the `Selection` build. `Extent` names no field, so the label is unchanged.

summary: A one-clause engine Selection is built six ways across four suites, and the shared home is the least capable of the six — the Selection twin of the fold 18c81f2d shipped.

tests.asserts: the reachability suite's 12 bound-selection proofs hold unchanged with every selection built through the one home, including the guidance-carrying and advisory-severity cases
the reached-from opt-in guard still walks nothing under a foreign predicate and indicts the member outside the closure under the declared clause, with both selections built through the one home

acceptance: `cargo test` green with one home building every one-clause engine `Selection` in the `it` crate, the label of each derived from its selector rather than hand-spelled, no call site of `bound` or `root_reachable_binding` moved, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean of the imports the folded literals strand.
notes: Out of scope by the crate boundary: `src/engine.rs:2435`'s `kind_selection` is the same job for in-src unit tests, which cannot reach the `it` crate's `common` — `src/test_support.rs` is `pub(crate)` and the per-crate fixture wrapper is the sanctioned split. It is a caller of that module's own `clause`, which FIXTURE-CLAUSE-LABEL-IS-THE-SHIPPED-ADDRESS owns; the two entries are file-disjoint. scoped at 8d0d2fd2
